fatal_errors: The proposed direct-coexistence/interface-pinning route does not reconstruct the target MTP-assisted free-energy perturbation method and cannot be assumed to provide DFT-level free energies solely because the potential was trained on DFT data.
The cited evidence only establishes general interest in refractory high-entropy alloys and does not support the claimed melting methodology, accuracy, or computational savings.
explanation: The hypothesis correctly identifies DFT-trained machine-learning interatomic potentials as a way to reduce the cost of refractory-material melting calculations and provides a useful head-to-head validation experiment. However, it omits the central methodological advance: using a high-fidelity moment tensor potential as the reference for rapidly convergent free-energy perturbation to DFT, replacing EAM-based thermodynamic integration. It also fails to identify TaVCrW, the specified pressure, temperature range, supercell, functionals, training accuracy, electronic free-energy contribution, or short-range-order stabilization. Its generic <10% accuracy criterion and unspecified cost reduction do not match the reported sub-0.5 meV/atom agreement, 80% savings, or melting-temperature shifts. The boundary discussion captures training-set dependence but misses the magnetic, SRO, and functional-related limitations.
